title: RAW_UNREVIEWED: multilingual medical prose through one shared consonantal script channel
summary: Retain a whole-reading architecture motivated by Hebrew and Judaeo-Arabic medical witnesses: one globally shared script-to-cipher map, with paragraph-level language choice and language-specific morphology. Cambridge identifies Avicenna witnesses T-S Ar.11.19 in Judaeo-Arabic and T-S NS90.75 in Hebrew; T-S K14.22 independently attests Syriac medical language in Jewish Aramaic characters. No source collation, model selection or manuscript gate has passed.

design.mechanism: A common written consonantal repertoire can carry several different languages. Infer one injective, globally prefix-free map from source script units to one-/two-symbol ciphertext strings, jointly with complete word readings and a single latent language per predeclared paragraph. Language changes select a source-derived lexical/morphological grammar, never a different cipher key. Preserve source-attested vowel letters; do not manufacture vowel deletion from modern vocalized spellings. No per-word language assignment, null codes, invented cognates or local repairs.
design.unit: Complete paragraphs and their entire words; one language assignment per fixed paragraph, one key across all paragraphs. Historical sources motivate this architecture, not a claim that these particular fragments were copied into the Voynich manuscript.
design.contrast: Joint multilingual common-script reconstruction versus each fixed single-language model with the identical channel family. The unknown is whether cross-language full-word and morphological constraints leave a unique shared reading, or permit unrelated language/key explanations. This is not retrieval from anonymous graphs.
design.prediction: Every surviving model must read complete held paragraphs and novel word forms under the same already learned script map; minority-language paragraphs must constrain and be constrained by that map. Report all surviving complete plaintext projections and unresolved equivalences. Unobserved parameters get no identification credit.

primary_sources.verified_catalogue_fact: Cambridge identifies a Judaeo-Arabic fragment of Avicenna's Canon, Book III, concerning sleep disorders; Egypt, 11th–13th century.
Cambridge identifies a Hebrew translation of the anatomical section of Avicenna's Canon; Italy or France, 15th–16th century.

The identifying scholar describes an alphabetically organized Syriac materia-medica text transcribed into Jewish Aramaic characters, with occasional Palestinian vowel signs. This is a script/language distinction example, not an automatic third-language fit pool.
Cambridge explicitly defines Judaeo-Arabic as Arabic language in Hebrew script and distinguishes Hebrew translations.

novelty_vs_predecessors.GDT892: 892 selects one Latin orthographic abugida with inherent vowel, carrier and virama and ITTB grammar. Proposed mechanism instead shares an attested consonantal writing repertoire across different language grammars; no inherent-vowel CV scanner. 892's insufficient control source remains closed, not repaired by this proposal.
novelty_vs_predecessors.GDT893: 893 has one whole-word bijection and exact source windows. Here the shared parameters are script units, so new inflected forms and different languages can constrain one another without receiving independent whole-word keys. Merely adding Genizah source windows to893 would not implement this architecture.
novelty_vs_predecessors.GDT341_343: These calibrated anonymous/persistent-identity recipe graph retrieval and did not reconstruct full source spellings under a jointly constrained multilingual script channel. Their failed comparator gates remain unchanged.

known_blockers_for_experimental_selectio: No complete independently collated source transcription pool frozen; library captions are catalogue evidence, not the required text corpus.

Common script-unit inventory, positional letter forms, dots/vocalization and spelling variation have not been measured and frozen; source-dependent normalization could otherwise smuggle in separate keys.
Language grammars and attested orthographic word analyses missing; Hebrew and Judaeo-Arabic semantic similarities are not literal spelling identities.
The cited fragments do not demonstrate language switching within one original manuscript or share one time/place. Historical plurality motivates a raw architecture only.
No adequate independent blinded control, held capacity, exact search completeness or manuscript contract established. No experiment selected.
design.retention_vs_selection: Missing collation and channel specification block experimental selection, not preservation of this diverse raw architecture. Before implementation, write a new bounded decision note after source predecessors are checked; do not automatically start a decoder or substitute a corpus for failed892.
design.duplicate_review: Registry multilingual/Genizah searches and declared-design duplicate screen found no same declared design; lexical ranking is navigation only. Primary341–343 comparator reports inspected. Broader old language/decoder predecessors still require targeted review before selection.
design.exposure: Official Cambridge text pages/catalogue descriptions only; no manuscript images, Voynich target data, private models or public decipherment searches.
